quandoUsar: A preview that switches between landscape, square, and portrait (a crop format selector, for example) without layout shift.
Reserve the space of an image, video, or `iframe` before loading, with the media cropped from the center.
Vertical formats that should not push the page: with `maxHeight` the box narrows instead of growing.
quandoEvitar: When the ratio never changes and there is no cropping, the CSS `aspect-ratio` property does the job without a client component.
Use `image-compare` to compare two images with a divider.
Use `image-viewer` when photos need to open enlarged, with zoom and navigation.
acessibilidade: It is a `div` with no role or label: the description comes from the media you place inside, so provide `alt` on the image or `title` on the `iframe`.
movimento: When `ratio` changes, the ratio itself animates with a no-overshoot spring and the browser recalculates width and height on every frame, so the media never stretches as it would with a `scale`.
The first render does not animate; `animated={false}` swaps immediately, and with “reduce motion” the swap is always instant.
responsivo: The box takes 100% of the parent's width; with `maxHeight` the width becomes the smaller of 100% and `maxHeight` times the ratio, and the box is centered in the row.
desempenho: The animation touches layout, not `transform`: each frame recalculates the box and what comes after it, which is light for a preview and heavy for a whole grid changing ratio at the same time.
notasIA: `ratio` accepts a number (`16 / 9`) or text (`"16/9"`, `"16:9"`, `"1.85"`); an unreadable value falls back to 16:9 without a warning.

Direct children `img`, `video`, `canvas`, `iframe`, and `picture` are stretched over the box and cropped (`fit="contain"` shows the whole media); other children you position yourself, since the box is `position: relative`.
`onRatioSettled` fires when the box settles on a new ratio (it does not fire on mount); the parent must define the width.
